long_biography.plain_text:
At 10 rue Cassette in Saint-Germain-des-Pres, a seventeenth-century convent offered Pierre-Antoine Lafortune an unusual hospitality canvas. Working with decorator Michel Boyer, he preserved the garden and historic fabric while giving the rooms individual character. The resulting Hotel de l'Abbaye paired a domestic scale with attentive service, an approach that distinguished the property from standardised city accommodation.

Lafortune's role extended beyond one address. As a vice-president of the Paris hotel federation, he represented local operators within the regional trade. His family vehicle later consolidated ownership before the hotel changed hands, closing a long chapter of direct stewardship without erasing the founders' design legacy.
